MilkDrop on a Mac

Does MilkDrop work on Mac?

By Syd Lawrence, a visual artist and developer who makes Vibresia. Facts last checked 2 November 2026; updated 2 November 2026.

No. MilkDrop is a visualiser plug-in for Winamp on Windows, and its author's page lists Windows 98 through Windows 7 with no Mac version. You can still get its presets on a Mac with projectM, an open-source rebuild of MilkDrop, or skip the presets and use a visualiser made for the Mac.

What MilkDrop is

MilkDrop is the music visualiser Ryan Geiss wrote for Winamp. Its beat detection drives a huge range of effects, and it can follow a live feed such as a microphone or line-in, not just what Winamp is playing. Its author has published the source code for several versions.

Most of what people remember about MilkDrop is its presets. Each one is a small file of equations that describes how the picture should move and change with the music, and over the years the community wrote thousands of them. That turned out to matter more than the program itself: the presets have outlived Winamp, and they're the reason MilkDrop still gets searched for.

Why it won't run on a Mac

MilkDrop is a Windows plug-in, built for Winamp's plug-in system. A Mac can't load it, and there's no Mac build to download from its author. We haven't tested running Windows on a Mac to see whether MilkDrop works inside it, so we won't tell you it does.

So the question to ask is what you actually want from it. There are three answers, and each has a different route.

If you want the presets: projectM

projectM is a reimplementation of MilkDrop that plays the same presets on Mac, Windows and Linux. It's an open-source library (LGPL) that other apps build on, with its own apps on top, and its default pack has about ten thousand presets.

Be ready for a little setup. The Apple Music plug-in for macOS is an unsigned development preview. The macOS standalone apps are pre-releases or development previews; the Steam and Homebrew builds are an old 3.1.12 release. Its GitHub page lists each build and how finished it is.

Two other ways to see the presets on a Mac: ProjectMilkSyphon, a Mac app from Vidvox built on projectM, which can capture audio straight from apps like Music or Safari; and Butterchurn, which runs the presets in a web browser.

If you want a visualiser that feels like it belongs on a Mac

If what you miss is having something hypnotic moving to the music, rather than MilkDrop's exact look, a native app may suit you better. Vibresia, which we make, listens to the Mac's system audio, so it reacts to Spotify, Apple Music, a browser or a film without a plug-in. It has 18 built-in scenes, it's free and open source, and you can write a new scene as a single GLSL function, or describe one to an AI assistant and have it written. It doesn't play MilkDrop presets, and it needs macOS 14.2 or later, Apple silicon.

If your music is all in the Music app, Apple's own visualiser is already there: play a song, then choose Window, then Visualizer. A song has to be playing in the Music app; it doesn't visualise Spotify, a browser or other apps.

If you want it for a live set

If you play visuals for other people, on a Mac ProjectMilkSyphon is the closest match: it sends its picture over Syphon so VJ software can mix it in. On Windows, NestDrop builds a VJ tool around the MilkDrop engine, but it doesn't run on a Mac either.

For a side-by-side of all of these, with prices, see MilkDrop alternatives for Mac.

Questions people ask

Is there a Mac version of Winamp's MilkDrop?

No. MilkDrop's author lists Windows versions only. projectM is the open-source rebuild that plays its presets on a Mac.

Can I use MilkDrop presets on a Mac?

Yes, with projectM, ProjectMilkSyphon or Butterchurn. All three play MilkDrop's preset files.

What's the easiest MilkDrop-like visualiser to install on a Mac?

If you want the presets, ProjectMilkSyphon is a ready-made Mac app. If you don't need the presets, Vibresia is a free signed app that listens to whatever the Mac is playing.
